# Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion

## Problem statement

Pi agent sessions launched in Herdr panes run `pi` in **interactive** mode with
an initial prompt (`packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`). When a skill
completes it emits a `</end_session>` marker, but nothing consumes that marker:
the interactive REPL simply waits for the next input, so the pane and its
~200 MB pi process stay alive forever. Over hours these abandoned sessions
accumulate — the operator observed **50 concurrent pi sessions / ~12.4 GB RSS
with ages up to 18+ hours**, contributing to severe CPU oversubscription
(load ~3× cores). Nothing transitions the session to a closed state on skill
completion, and there is no lifecycle hook that reaps sessions whose agent died
without emitting the marker.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — wants completed agent panes to disappear on their
  own so the machine is not oversubscribed and panes do not need manual pruning.
- **Downtime dispatcher** — spawns intake/plan/audit/risk-effort panes for every
  dispatched item; if those panes never close, the dispatcher floods the host.
- **Agents** — need their session to end cleanly (lease released, pane torn
  down) once their task and report are complete, without an operator click.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when a dispatched `/skill:intake` or `/skill:plan` session
  finishes and writes its `</end_session>` report, I want the pane to close
  automatically so idle sessions do not accumulate.
- As a producer, I want an agent that stops to ask me a question (no
  `</end_session>`) to keep its pane open so I can answer it, but an agent whose
  process died silently to be cleaned up.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — graceful auto-exit on completion.** When a pi run settles
   (`agent_settled`) and the final assistant message's concatenated text,
   `.rstrip()`-ed, ends with `</end_session>`, the Worklog pi extension requests
   an orderly shutdown (`ctx.shutdown()`) so the process exits, the pane is torn
   down, and the proxy model lease is released. Metric: a unit test with a
   fixture session whose last assistant text ends with the marker asserts
   `ctx.shutdown()` is called exactly once; an end-to-end check shows the pane
   closes within ~5 s of the report being emitted.
2. **AC2 — no false positives.** No shutdown is requested when the final
   assistant message does not end with the marker — including a `</end_session>`
   quoted mid-message, a question-ended session, an aborted run, and a run that
   ended in a non-retryable error. Metric: negative-path unit tests for each
   case assert zero `ctx.shutdown()` calls, and an item with
   `needsProducerReview=true` is never auto-closed.
3. **AC3 — marker-less sessions are reaped (fail-closed).** Sessions whose agent
   died or was killed without emitting the marker do not linger indefinitely: a
   liveness/idle reaper closes panes whose agent process is gone or idle beyond
   a configurable threshold (default to be set in planning), while **never**
   closing a pane that is actively working, has live child processes, or has
   `needsProducerReview=true`. Metric: table-driven classifier tests plus an
   integration check on a synthetic abandoned pane.
4. **AC4 — `implement` panes remain excluded** from automatic close, preserving
   the AC6 precedent of `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` unless the producer explicitly
   changes the policy. Metric: a test asserts an `implement` pane is never
   auto-closed.
5. **AC5 — child processes are not orphaned.** When a session exits or is
   terminated, its spawned children (e.g. audit/plan runners) are terminated
   with it, so none are reparented to PID 1. Metric: an integration test spawns
   a long-running child in a session-scoped process group, terminates the
   session, and asserts the child does not survive.
6. **AC6 — one shared idle/completion classifier.** The automatic hook and the
   `pane-triage` skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`) consume a single
   marker-detection + liveness helper, so the two mechanisms cannot diverge.
   Metric: both call the shared module; its classifier is covered by
   table-driven tests (marker at end accepted; marker mid-message rejected).
7. **AC7 — tests and documentation.** Unit and integration tests are added for
   every path. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/tui/extensions/README.md`, and any
   relevant `docs/` entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- Must not close a pane that is actively working **or** awaiting a producer
  answer.
- Must not break the existing `agent_end` recovery/compaction flow: the
  completion hook must run only at `agent_settled` (the point at which Pi will
  not continue automatically).
- The existing downtime auto-close logic (`pane-lifecycle.ts`,
  `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN`) must remain intact and must not double-handle or race
  the new in-process hook.
- Auto-close must be configurable/overridable (threshold, on/off) so an operator
  can disable it without editing code.
- Headless modes (JSON/RPC) must be unaffected; gate UI-facing behaviour to TUI
  mode as `herdr-agent-state.ts` already does.
- Never close the invoking/current operator pane.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` runs `pi` (interactive) with an
  initial prompt; on `pi` exit its `EXIT` trap calls
  `release-lease-on-exit.mjs` and Herdr tears the pane down when the primary
  process exits. **The gap is that `pi` never exits.**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/` is the auto-loaded pi extension
  (`index.ts` wires activity indicator, model display, session health,
  guardrails, skill-path, recovery, lease release). It already hooks
  `agent_end`, `session_shutdown`, `agent_start`/`agent_settled`-adjacent
  lifecycle events, so the completion hook belongs here.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` inspects
  the last assistant message on `agent_end` — a precedent for reading final
  output, and a coordination point so recovery finishes before shutdown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` classifies **dispatched** panes by
  worklog stage and closes everything except `implement`; it only covers panes
  recorded in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, so manually opened and
  marker-less panes are never reaped.
- `~/.pi/agent/extensions/herdr-agent-state.ts` reports `idle`/`working`/
  `blocked` to Herdr but never closes anything.
- The report helper (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  appends the canonical `</end_session>` marker and is emitted by every skill's
  end-of-session report.
- Observed evidence: 44–50 live `pi` processes (~200 MB RSS each), sessions with
  completed work still alive, and orphaned `audit_runner` children reparented to
  PID 1.

## Desired change

Add a session-completion lifecycle hook to the Worklog pi extension:

1. On `agent_settled`, read the final assistant message; if its trimmed text
   ends with `</end_session>`, call `ctx.shutdown()` (idempotent, once per
   session) so `pi` exits and the pane/lease is released.
2. Add a fail-closed liveness/idle safety net for sessions whose agent died
   without the marker (exact mechanism/placement to be settled in planning —
   in-extension watcher vs. extending `pane-lifecycle.ts`).
3. Ensure session-scoped child processes are terminated on teardown so none are
   orphaned to PID 1.
4. Extract the marker-detection + liveness classifier into a single shared
   helper reused by the automatic hook and `pane-triage`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` — register the new session-close module.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/session-close.ts` — **new**: marker detection + `agent_settled` → `ctx.shutdown()` + liveness fallback.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/session-close.test.ts` — **new**: positive/negative marker and reaper tests.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — existing `agent_end` lifecycle wiring; coordinate ordering so recovery completes before shutdown.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — external reaper classification (if the liveness fallback lives in herdr rather than the extension).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — pane-lifecycle monitor wiring; de-duplicate/sequence against the new in-process hook.
- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — verify the exit/lease-release path needs no change (reference only).
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document the new lifecycle hook and its configuration.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py` — reference only (marker source).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `</end_session>` is the single canonical terminal signal and
  is always the final line of a completed skill report.
- **Risk — premature shutdown.** Calling `ctx.shutdown()` at `agent_end` could
  race recovery/compaction; mitigated by using `agent_settled` (the documented
  no-further-automatic-work boundary).
- **Risk — false-positive close** of an interactive session mid-conversation;
  mitigated by strict final-message marker matching plus negative-path tests.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Orphaned-child reaping and the marker-less reaper
  overlap existing work; if either grows large it should become a child item
  rather than inflate this fix.
- **Risk — double handling.** The downtime `pane-lifecycle` monitor may race
  the new hook; both must be idempotent and the winner must be deterministic.
- **Risk — mode coverage.** `ctx.shutdown()` behaviour differs across TUI/JSON/
  RPC modes; gate the hook to TUI mode unless proven safe elsewhere.

## Related work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill: gated close of idle panes (manual complement; deferral question, see Appendix).
- `WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN` — Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement (precedent; `implement` exception).
- `WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN` — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception.
- `WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB` — Herdr plugin: release the Local Proxy model lease when a pi session is closed (exit/release path).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates performance pressure (orphaned audit_runners, stale servers).
- `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM).
- `WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO` — Fix orphaned ContextHub node processes that never exit after worktree cleanup.
- `WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O` — Auto-continue after mid-session compaction (session lifecycle precedent).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Deferral to the pane-triage skill (`WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`).**
  Should this item defer to pane-triage, or own the automatic lifecycle fix?
  **Recommended:** Keep both, but this item owns the automatic completion hook;
  pane-triage remains the approval-gated manual complement. Rationale:
  pane-triage's idle test is the same `</end_session>` marker and it never
  closes anything unattended, so it cannot prevent accumulation (the observed
  50 sessions/18h accumulated despite the operator being available), and it is
  blind to sessions whose agent died without emitting the marker.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer confirmation.
- **Q2 — Marker-less / crashed sessions.**
  Is a gated manual close sufficient, or is an automatic liveness/idle reaper
  required? **Recommended:** automatic, fail-closed reaper (AC3), because
  marker-less sessions are invisible to pane-triage and dominated the observed
  backlog. **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer confirmation.
- **Q3 — Orphaned child-process cleanup (AC5) scope.**
  In scope here or a separate child item? **Recommended:** keep AC5 in this item
  if it stays small; otherwise split a child item (the audit runner lives in the
  SorraAgents `skill/audit` tree, outside this repo). **OPEN QUESTION** —
  awaiting producer confirmation.
- **Q4 — Does `</end_session>` align with the session-close lifecycle?**
  **Answer (agent research):** Partially. It is the correct primary signal for
  graceful completions, but the pane-triage model misses sessions that died
  without emitting it. Evidence: live idle `pi` REPLs with completed work, plus
  `audit_runner` children reparented to PID 1 (parent died, no marker).
  Source: process inspection, `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/*`,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP** – Show complete, right-aligned model name on footer Line 3 (remove 30-col truncation) (completed)
- **WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514** – Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating (completed)
- **WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO** – In-flight guard: Herdr-head and normal scan paths (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0msgi7uih008usvb, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+350 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: aborted, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac5 (+293 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: actively, add, added, agent, agents (+280 more)

# Retention sweep script with `--check` and unit tests

Deliver a stdlib-only, repo-local retention sweep that discovers stale
`audit_debug_*.jsonl` forensic dumps on this host and removes those that exceed
an age or size threshold. Conventions are mirrored from the SorraAgents audit
skill's `cleanup_debug_logs.py`, which is **referenced, not forked**
(repo-boundary rule: do not edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` or `skill/audit`).

## Scope

- New `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` (executable, standard library only).
- Discovery: every `~/projects/*/.worklog/` store (files directly in the store —
  non-recursive, so worktree sub-directories are not swept) and
  `~/.audit_debug/**` (recursive). Repeatable `--root <path>` overrides make
  discovery testable against a `tmp_path` tree.
- Name guard: only files whose basename matches `audit_debug_*.jsonl` are ever
  considered. `worklog.db`, `worklog.db-wal`, `worklog.db-shm`, `config.yaml`,
  worktrees and every other file are never selected.
- Selection: a candidate is selected when its `mtime` is strictly older than
  `--older-than` days (default 7) **or** its size is strictly greater than
  `--max-size` MB (default 50).
- Modes: dry-run is the default (prints the selected set and aggregate bytes);
  `--apply` deletes the selected set; `--check` deletes nothing and exits
  non-zero when the remaining debug-log footprint exceeds `--budget-gb`
  (default 5).
- Robustness: an `OSError` on stat/unlink skips that file and continues (the
  sweep never aborts mid-set); every removed file emits one audit line
  (path + bytes) to stdout and, when `--log-file` is given, to an append-only
  log.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` is a standalone stdlib-only executable Python 3 script whose discovery finds `audit_debug_*.jsonl` directly under each `~/projects/*/.worklog/` store and recursively under `~/.audit_debug/**`, honours `--root` overrides, returns no candidates for a missing root, and documents every flag and default in `--help`.
2. Selection is name-guarded to `audit_debug_*.jsonl` and selects only files strictly older than `--older-than` days (default 7) OR strictly larger than `--max-size` MB (default 50); all other files are never selected or deleted.
3. Dry-run is the default and changes nothing on disk; `--apply` deletes exactly the selected set, emits one audit line per removed file (path + bytes), and a second `--apply` immediately afterwards reports zero candidates.
4. `--check` deletes nothing, exits 0 when the remaining debug-log footprint is within `--budget-gb` (default 5), and exits non-zero when it exceeds that budget.
5. An `OSError` while stat-ing or unlinking a candidate is logged and skipped — the sweep continues and still processes the remaining candidates.
6. `pytest tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` passes and covers the age boundary (just inside/outside), size boundary (just under/over), non-matching-name safety, missing-root no-op, dry-run no-op, `--apply` exact set, `--check` under/over-budget exit codes, second-apply idempotence, and OSError skip-and-continue.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — new: discovery, selection, dry-run/`--apply`/`--check`
- `tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — new: pytest coverage driven by `tmp_path`

## Notes

Write the tests first (TDD); the item is complete only when the whole module is
green. The `.worklog/*` path is git-ignored in this repo, so no tracked data is
affected.

Implementation (TDD): added `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` and `tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py`.

Design: default discovery = every `~/projects/*/.worklog` store (non-recursive, worktrees excluded) + `~/.audit_debug` (recursive); repeatable `--root` overrides (a path named `.worklog` is non-recursive, others recursive). Selection is name-guarded to `audit_debug_*.jsonl` and picks files strictly older than `--older-than` days (default 7) OR strictly larger than `--max-size` MB (default 50). Dry-run is default; `--apply` deletes the exact set and emits one audit line (path + bytes) per removed file (also appended to `--log-file`); `--check` deletes nothing and exits 1 when the total footprint exceeds `--budget-gb` (default 5). `OSError` on stat/unlink is logged and skipped, never aborting the sweep.

Verification: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py -q` -> 15 passed. ruff check clean. Dry-run against real host state reports 20882 candidates / 26151 discovered; `--check` reports 24.63 GB footprint (over the 5 GB budget, exit 1). No files were modified.
